caption_en:
One country against nine. Watch the rope. 🪢

1 Israeli vs 9 countries. Who wins the GDP tug of war? 🪢

GDP per person, 2024 (US$):
🇮🇱 Israel: 54,291
🇾🇪 Yemen: 442
🇸🇾 Syria: 1,057 (World Bank, 2022, latest)
🇱🇧 Lebanon: 5,248
🇮🇷 Iran: 4,834
🇪🇬 Egypt: 3,594
🇯🇴 Jordan: 5,003
🇮🇶 Iraq: 6,388
🇹🇷 Turkey: 15,914
🇴🇲 Oman: 20,529

8 countries together: 42,480. Israel holds.
Swap Turkey for Oman: 47,095. Still Israel.
All 9 together: 63,009. Only then they win.

Adding up per-person numbers is a playful scoreboard, not an economic statistic. It shows the size of the gap.
War and sanctions hold Yemen and Syria back, and oil lifts the Gulf. This is about economies, not about anyone being less.

ישראלי אחד מול 9 מדינות. תוצר לנפש, 2024: ישראל 54,291. שמונה מדינות ביחד: 42,480, וישראל מחזיקה. רק כשכל ה 9 מושכים ביחד, 63,009, הם מנצחים.

Sources: IMF World Economic Outlook, Oct 2026, GDP per capita (NGDPDPC), 2024. Syria: World Bank, NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, 2022.
Made with AI tools.
AI voice (Noam's own cloned voice) on the new opening.

lines.line: In this corner, Israel, $54,000. And in the other corner, Yemen and Syria, plus Lebanon, plus Iran, plus Egypt, plus Jordan, plus Iraq, plus Turkey, eight count

transcript.heard: $54,000 against 9 countries. In this corner, Israel, $54,000. And in the other corner, Yemen and Syria, plus Lebanon, plus Iran, plus Egypt, plus Jordan, plus Iraq, plus Turkey. 8 countries, 42,000 together, and Israel holds. Okay, let's swap Turkey for Oman, 47,000, still Israel. Fine. Everyone together, 63,000. Finally, Israel slides over the line. It took a team of nine to out pull one Israeli. That's how hard Israelis work, building for themselves and for the world. War and sanctions hold Yemen and Syria back and oil lifts the Gulf. Ready for the rematch? Same rope.
